note: Curated HR interview questions with answer guidance (what the interviewer expects, points to cover, structure, mistakes). General guidance, not company-specific. Personal details are only ever taken from the candidate's own resume.

questions.question: Tell me about yourself.
questions.expects: A short, relevant professional introduction that connects your background to this role - not your life story.
points: Your current studies or role
Two or three skills most relevant to the role
One project or experience that shows those skills
Why you are interested in this role now
structure: Present: who you are and what you study or do
Past: the project or experience that best shows your skills
Future: what you want to do next and why this role fits
mistakes: Reciting your whole resume line by line
Personal details unrelated to the job
Speaking for more than about two minutes
Claiming skills you cannot discuss in depth

questions.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
questions.expects: Self-awareness: real strengths backed by evidence, and a genuine weakness you are actively improving.
points: One or two strengths with a concrete example each
A real, non-critical weakness
What you are doing to improve it and the progress so far
structure: Strength + evidence from a project or course
Concrete improvement steps and a result
mistakes: Disguised strengths such as 'I work too hard'
A weakness that is a core requirement of the role
Strengths with no evidence

questions.question: Where do you see yourself in the next few years?
questions.expects: Direction and commitment: goals that are realistic and connected to the role and the company.
points: The skills you want to deepen
The kind of responsibility you want to grow into
How this role is a step towards that
structure: Short-term: what you want to learn in this role
Medium-term: the contribution you want to make
mistakes: Saying you plan to leave soon for something unrelated
Vague answers such as 'somewhere good'
Goals that ignore the role you applied for

questions.question: Why should we hire you?
questions.expects: A clear match between the role's needs and your evidence-backed skills.
points: The two or three requirements of the role you meet best
Evidence for each from your projects or experience
What you would contribute or learn quickly
structure: Match each need with your evidence
Close with your motivation and readiness to learn
mistakes: Comparing yourself with other candidates
Generic claims with no evidence
Overstating experience

questions.question: Why are you interested in this role?
questions.expects: Genuine, informed motivation for this kind of work.
points: What attracts you to the work itself
Related projects or courses you enjoyed
What you hope to learn
structure: Evidence you have already explored it
What you want to learn next
mistakes: Talking only about salary or perks
Not knowing what the role involves
A generic answer that fits any job

questions.question: Tell me about a time you worked in a team. What was your role?
questions.expects: Collaboration and communication, with your own contribution made clear.
points: The team goal
Your specific responsibility
How you communicated and handled disagreements
The outcome
structure: Action (what you did and how you coordinated)
mistakes: Only saying 'we' so your contribution is unclear
Blaming teammates
No outcome

questions.question: Walk me through a project you are proud of.
questions.expects: Depth: you understand the problem, your decisions and their trade-offs, and the result.
points: The problem and who it was for
Your design and technology choices and why
A difficulty you solved
The result and what you would improve
structure: Challenge and how you solved it
mistakes: Listing technologies without explaining decisions
Taking credit for others' work
Being unable to answer follow-up questions about your own code

questions.question: Tell me about a difficult problem you solved. How did you approach it?
questions.expects: A structured way of thinking: how you understood the problem, explored options and checked the result.
points: What made the problem hard
How you broke it down or researched it
The options you considered and why you chose one
How you verified the result and what you learned
structure: Situation and why it was difficult
mistakes: Choosing a trivial problem
Skipping how you reached the solution
Taking credit for a team's work without saying so

questions.question: What would you do if you realised you could not finish a task by its deadline?
questions.expects: Ownership, early communication and sensible prioritisation.
points: Tell the right person early
Explain the reason and what is already done
Offer options: reduced scope, more time, help
Prevent it next time
mistakes: Hiding the problem until the deadline
Delivering low-quality work silently
Blaming others

questions.question: How would you handle being asked to use a technology you have never used?
questions.expects: A structured, independent approach to learning and asking for help at the right time.
points: Start with official documentation and a small prototype
Time-box learning and ask for help when stuck
Example of learning something quickly before
structure: Explain how you would confirm your work is right
mistakes: Saying you would refuse or wait for training
Claiming you would never need help

questions.question: How would you explain a technical concept to someone without a technical background?
questions.expects: Clear communication: choosing the right level of detail for the audience.
points: Find out what the listener already knows
Use an analogy or example
Check understanding and invite questions
structure: Pick a concept from your work
Explain how you would check they understood
mistakes: Using jargon
Talking down to the listener
Not checking understanding
